identity.source: packet captures of the app + live polling against one unit; see docs/astral/CONTEXTO.md (not published with this repo)

notes: Heat-only pump: no mode byte exists on this wire, so `modes` is just ["heat"] and the climate entity keeps Home Assistant's own 8-40C bounds/0.5 step (no per-pump min/max register to read). `outputs.compressor` (D0/1 byte 6 bit 0) and `outputs.fan` (bit 3) are confirmed by measuring power at the pump's own outlet while it was on the network: ~7W idle, ~120W with only the fan bit set, ~1826W with the compressor bit set, and the fan bit coming on first with the compressor following ~64s later across two observed cycles. `fan_alt` (D0/0 group 0x4F byte 7, a second, independent source for the same physical fan) is also confirmed: it agreed with outputs.fan on every observed state (fan on and off) with zero mismatches. The Fan running diagnostic entity still reads outputs.fan as the primary value and surfaces fan_alt as an attribute (`mismatch_with_primary`) only if a future reading ever disagrees — now a disagreement alert, not an expected occurrence. `outputs.outputs_5_6` (bit 4) and `alarm` (D0/0 group 0x53 byte 5) remain probable, not confirmed by this round of testing. D0/0 group 0x4F bytes 5-6 (besides byte 7) and the exact inlet-vs-outlet byte assignment (D0/1 bytes 1/2) remain unconfirmed and intentionally unmapped. The entity/device is reported unavailable only until page 80/1 and page D0/1 have both been seen at least once; compressor, fan, fan_alt, and alarm (all tied to D0/1 byte 6 or the D0/0 groups) simply read as unknown until their own source frame arrives, without that holding back the rest of the device — no field ever shows a guessed off/false/idle before its real source frame arrives. Pages 80/6 and 80/7 (plaintext Wi-Fi password) are never read by the driver, not just unmapped here. All MAC/CRC bytes in fixtures.frames are fabricated, not from a real capture.
